subject: Streaming token contours & max-output tradeoffs — post-demo ops checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@tidebank.com>; TideBank Platform Team <platform@tidebank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: streaming vs max-output tradeoffs + immediate asks

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the TideBank platform crew. High-level recap and suggested next steps so we have a single place to iterate.

Summary of what we heard (from your side):
- Primary goal: serve real-time chat assistants within TideBank apps with sub-300ms p95 user-visible latency for short replies (<= 128 output tokens).
- Secondary flows: longer, policy-augmented answers (300–800 output tokens) for back-office agents; those can be higher latency but need predictable throughput.
- Expected steady-state traffic for pilot: ~150 QPS, peak bursts to ~400 QPS, concurrency per model ~40–60.
- Most messages are short (median input 40 tokens), but 10–15% of sessions will include long context (history + PDF extracts) pushing input to 6–8k tokens.

Open/clarifying items we promised to validate:
1) Concrete latency SLO for long-response flow (we suggested p95 <= 2s as initial guardrail).
2) Whether TideBank can provide anonymized sample payloads (representative long-context requests) for a perf run.
3) Desired fallbacks: is it acceptable to return incremental/streamed partial outputs for long responses, or must final complete text be atomic?

Quick actions we propose (owner in parens):
- Run two targeted perf profiles against your sample payloads: 1) low-latency short outputs (<=128 tokens), 2) long-context streaming (up to 800 tokens) (Dev).
- Provide a recommended routing policy that hedges cost vs latency (tiered models + streaming) and a fallback plan for bursts (Marissa).
- Share the perf matrix and recording from today (attached) and a lightweight ingest template for sample payloads (Dev).

Attachment: perf-matrix.csv (summary rows for p50/p95/p99 across sequence lengths and concurrency), demo-recording-20271209.mp4

Next sync: propose Wed 2027-12-15 10:00 PT to review perf runs and pick pilot SLAs. Let me know if that works.

Thanks,
--
Marissa Cole

From: Alyssa Kim <alyssa.kim@tidebank.com>

Cc: TideBank Platform Team <platform@tidebank.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2027 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: streaming vs max-output tradeoffs + immediate asks

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Short-reply SLO: we need p95 <= 250ms in-app for the chat ribbon flow (we mostly surface the assistant inline). Anything above that leads to poor UX.
2) For long answers (agent-facing), we can tolerate p95 <= 3s for full outputs as long as partial streaming is available so the agent sees early content.
3) Bursts: banking peak windows are predictable (month-end reports) and can be very spiky; we need an autoscale hedging approach rather than hard throttling.

We'll assemble an anonymized sample set — two buckets: short chats (~2k samples) and long-context cases (~300 samples with attached PDF extracts). We'll push a ZIP to your Drive link by EOD Friday.

Also: question on model fallbacks — would Redwood do region-level fallback to a slightly cheaper quantized variant automatically? We want to understand quality tradeoffs.

Alyssa
Alyssa Kim
Head of Platform, TideBank
alyssa.kim@tidebank.com

On Thu, Dec 9, 2027 at 09:02 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:

Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 08:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: streaming vs max-output tradeoffs + immediate asks

Appreciate the specificity, Alyssa — that helps a lot. Short answers: p95 <= 250ms is aggressive but achievable with the right model routing and prefix caching. Long answers: streaming partials + p95 <= 3s for complete output is a good baseline.

Pilot plan (high level):
- Perf runs (Dev) — we'll run three microbenchmarks against your sample set:
  * Short-path: median input 40 tokens, target output 64–128 tokens, concurrency up to 60 — measure p50/p95/p99.
  * Long-context streaming: inputs 4k–8k tokens, outputs up to 800 tokens, concurrency 10–20 (streaming enabled).
  * Burst stress: synthetic ramp to 400 QPS for 5m to validate autoscale and fallback behavior.
- Expected observations and hedges:
  * For short-path, expect p95 in 120–260ms range depending on per-request batching and KV cache hit rate. We can push lower by reducing per-request batch windows at a modest cost uplift.
  * For long-context, expect single-token-step latency to grow with KV-cache size; end-to-end complete-output p95 will likely be in 1.5–4s depending on model variant and streaming chunk size.
  * We recommend enabling streaming with 128-token chunk emissions for agent flows to improve perceived latency; allow finalization flush to ensure deterministic output.
- Routing recommendations:
  1) Default to low-latency model for short-path with prefix cache pinned to frequent system prompts.
  2) Route long-context to a memory-optimized variant with KV caching and incremental streaming. If under heavy bursts, automatically route 20% of traffic to a quantized fallback with lower cost (quality guardrails in place).

Attached: perf-matrix.csv (first pass). I'll coordinate with Dev on the perf runs next.

Alyssa — are there specific quality thresholds (BLEU / synthetic eval or manual markers) you want us to use when comparing fallback quantized models to the full model? That will determine how aggressive we are on routing.

Cheers,
--
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: perf-run plan + data access request (TideBank)

Internal note — runbook and asks from TideBank: we need the anonymized samples (Alyssa said EOD Friday) and two quick creds: S3 read-only bucket or secure Drive link for payloads, and a representative Doc ID for the long-context PDFs so we can exercise real tokenization.

Planned perf steps (timeline):
- Day 0: ingest samples, generate synthetic variants (token-extending) to simulate worst-case KV sizes.
- Day 1: short-path microbench (multi-concurrency sweep 10/30/60), collect p50/p95/p99, tokenization distribution.
- Day 2: long-context streaming runs, evaluate perceived latency (first-chunk time) and completion time; try chunk sizes 64/128/256.
- Day 3: burst stress test (ramp to 400 QPS), confirm autoscale and canary fallback routing.

Deliverables: perf report (CSV), recommended routing policy (YAML), and a short decisions doc for the pilot SLA. I'll upload artifacts to the Drive folder listed in the thread.

If Ben or Marissa want to surface any additional success metrics (e.g., first-byte time target for streaming vs overall completion), flag them now.

Thanks,
